archetypes.name: architecture
archetypes.rationale: The awk TOML config-stripping in launch-codex-exec.sh and contract equivalence between the new codex/claude drafter launchers fall outside correctness and edge-cases scope.
archetypes.prompt_body: The diff introduces `scripts/launch-codex-drafter.sh` as a new drafter backend that must match the status KV contract of `scripts/launch-claude-drafter.sh` so that `skills/design/SKILL.md` Step 2b can treat both launchers identically downstream. Examine whether the new launcher's status KV fields, dirty-tree sidecar shape, and success/failure exit codes are strictly equivalent to the Claude path across all branches. Also review the awk TOML block-end matching in `scripts/launch-codex-exec.sh` for the `--trusted-instructions-file` path: the awk uses `index($0, block_end)` to detect the closing triple-quote line, which matches any line *containing* the delimiter substring rather than only an exact-delimiter line — assess whether this can prematurely terminate the skip block on legal TOML string body lines. Verify the `LARCH_DESIGN_DRAFTER` vendor selection logic in `skills/design/SKILL.md` covers all edge cases (invalid vendor, empty env var, `CODEX_PRESENT` unset or misspelled) and that the `codex-plan-draft` timing kind is wired consistently across `scripts/lib-timing-kinds.sh`, the launcher, and SKILL.md. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: robustness
archetypes.rationale: The EXIT trap's reliance on unset globals and cross-path temp-file cleanup in launch-codex-drafter.sh needs a deeper failure-path audit than the generic edge-cases reviewer provides.
archetypes.prompt_body: The new `scripts/launch-codex-drafter.sh` registers an EXIT trap (`write_dirty_tree_sidecar`) before `OUTPUT_CANON` and `DESIGN_CANON` are set, relying on `[[ -n "${OUTPUT_CANON:-}" ]] || return 0` as a guard. Audit whether every early-exit path (pre-canonicalization failures, invalid `--output-file` parent dir) reliably leaves `OUTPUT_CANON` unset so the guard fires correctly, and whether `DESIGN_CANON` is always set by the time the trap calls `git -C "$REPO_ROOT" status`. Also check temp file cleanup across all failure branches: `$_codex_raw`, `$_launcher_stdout`, `$_plan_tmp`, `$_summary_tmp`, and `$_trusted_instructions` are removed on the success path and some error paths — verify they are also cleaned up when the Python parse step fails (exit 99), when `launch-codex-exec.sh` itself crashes before writing `_launcher_stdout`, and in the CODEX_EMPTY_OUTPUT branch. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
